condition.name: ARC-sol
condition.notes: 维护者 2026-11-02 加（#185）：阶段一的 GPT-6.1 Sol 列。ARC 用自带的 OpenAI 兼容客户端（llm.provider=openai-compatible、wire_api=responses）经 codex-api 用 `codex-2`；ARC 没有 effort 设置，openai-route.patch 在每个请求里带 reasoning.effort（和 Anthropic 路线的 output_config.effort 补丁同理，只读观测之外唯一的改动）。ARC 各阶段的 max_tokens 在这条路线上不会被思考吃满（#106 的问题）：ARC 发的 max_output_tokens 和 temperature 都被 codex-api 在请求到 Codex 之前去掉，所以 #106 的问题在这条路线上不存在。 effort 为 medium，与其他条件的 high 不同（维护者 2026-11-04 定，#227）：经 ChatGPT 订阅（Codex 登录）线路，OpenAI 后端约在 900 s 时复位单个请求的流（codex-api 回 500，#223），ARC 第 10 阶段用一个请求生成全部实验代码，high 下常超过 15 分钟，被切后 ARC 重试同一请求又撞同一上限；降低 effort 是设定实验条件的请求参数（先例：ARC-opus，#106），不改 ARC 的提示、阶段和算法。
condition.notes_en: Added by the maintainer on 2026-11-02 (#185): the GPT-6.1 Sol column of phase 1. ARC uses its own OpenAI-compatible client (llm.provider=openai-compatible, wire_api=responses) through codex-api on `codex-2`; ARC has no effort setting, so openai-route.patch puts reasoning.effort on every request (as the output_config.effort patch does for the Anthropic route; apart from read-only logging the only change). ARC's per-stage max_tokens cannot be eaten by thinking on this route (the problem of #106): the max_output_tokens and temperature ARC sends are removed by codex-api before the request reaches Codex, so the problem of #106 does not exist on this route. Effort is medium, unlike the high of the other conditions (maintainer, 2026-11-04, #227): on the ChatGPT-subscription (Codex login) route OpenAI's backend resets a single request's stream at about 900 s (codex-api answers 500, #223); ARC stage 10 generates all the experiment code in one request, which at high often runs past 15 minutes, and after the cut ARC retries the same request into the same limit. Lowering the effort is a request parameter that sets the experiment condition (precedent: ARC-opus, #106); ARC's prompts, stages and algorithm are untouched.

meaning.en: AutoResearchClaw; provider openai, reasoning effort medium.

tools.permissions: no tool calls (requests carry model, messages, max_tokens); generated experiments run in experiment containers ARC starts (E2E tasks, docker mode) or as plain subprocesses in the container (benchmark items)

preinstalled.zh: python:3.11 bookworm；上游代码按 PYTHONPATH 使用；pdflatex + bibtex；CPU 版 PyTorch 和 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、pandas、matplotlib 等（constraints.txt 固定）；实验镜像另有 ARC 提示所列的 torchvision、transformers、datasets、h5py 等（experiment-constraints.txt 固定）
preinstalled.en: python:3.11 bookworm; upstream code via PYTHONPATH; pdflatex + bibtex; CPU PyTorch with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib and more (pinned by constraints.txt); the experiment image adds the torchvision, transformers, datasets, h5py and others the ARC prompt lists (experiment-constraints.txt)

notes.model: gpt-6.1-sol through the project's own ChatGPT (Codex) login on codex-api  (account ), ARC's OpenAI-compatible client with llm.provider=openai-compatible and wire_api=responses, no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. ARC sends model, input, max_output_tokens and (it sends it for every model that is not o3/o4) temperature; codex-api removes max_output_tokens and temperature before the request reaches Codex, so neither takes effect.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain model calls. conditions.agent=codex means only that the provider is the project's Codex login through codex-api; the Codex CLI is not involved. E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). ARC's entrypoint there installs requirements.txt, runs the generated setup.py (network through the shield: the task's data is downloaded here, into /workspace/data), cuts the network (iptables) and only then runs main.py. A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.experiment: E2E tasks run ARC's own docker mode (experiment.mode=docker, docker.network_policy=setup_only, #220): every generated experiment runs in a fresh container of the experiment image (the same CPU Python stack as ARC's image, started by ARC through the host docker socket, on the run's shield network, with the condition's cpus and memory). ARC's entrypoint there installs requirements.txt, runs the generated setup.py (network through the shield: the task's data is downloaded here, into /workspace/data), cuts the network (iptables) and only then runs main.py. A benchmark item keeps experiment.mode=sandbox (a plain subprocess in ARC's container, no network from the experiment's point of view: ARC's code-generation prompt for that mode forbids external data).
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; openai-route.patch sends reasoning.effort='medium' with every request (RWE_EFFORT). The per-stage max_tokens (4096, 8192, 16384) that the thinking of a Claude model eats up (#106) is not sent on this route (codex-api removes max_output_tokens), so thinking cannot starve a stage's text.
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. openai-route.patch appends each response's `usage` block and the request seconds to anthropic-usage.jsonl (the same log as the Messages API route); cost is not computed, there is no per-token charge on a ChatGPT plan.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s (in docker mode ARC passes it as the timeout of the whole container: pip install, setup.py and main.py), refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md with whitespace collapsed, in its faithful English version (candidate/TASK.en.md) when the task has one (#196: the keywords ARC's literature screen filters by are taken from the ASCII words of the topic, and a Chinese topic leaves only the file names it mentions); the run's result says which text it was (notes.topic_source). Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request is built in researchclaw/llm/client.py and carries only model, input, max_output_tokens, temperature and reasoning, never a tools or web_search field; web_search.enabled=false. The only host address the shield lets through is codex-api's model routes.
notes.secrets: An E2E task's experiments run in containers that get none of ARC's environment (only the shield's proxy variables and CA bundle). A benchmark item's experiment code runs as a subprocess and inherits the container environment: a placeholder key only (the shield proxy puts codex-api's local key on the request).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).
